name: turbocompressor_optimal_inlet
title: Teaching exercise: turbocompressor optimal speed and flow at a new inlet
summary: Teaching exercise on the optimal regime of a turbocompressor. With the two similarity constants given, the model computes the optimal rotation speed and suction volume flow for air at 0.9 bar and 50 °C discharging at 2.5 bar.

origin.course: ULiège, Machines et systèmes thermiques, repetition 4 (2004-10-12), exercise 5 continued

verification.summary: Compared with the EES stored solution of MSTH_041012_exercice_7_suite.EES: 13 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 0. Largest relative difference 5.06e-05 on V_dot_su; v_su prints the same 5.06e-05 (CoolProp Air specific volume 1.030541 m3/kg against the EES stored 1.030594 m3/kg). rpm and M_dot agree to about 1e-10. All 13 equations are satisfied.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of thermo_models TM-0060 (MSTH_041012_exercice_7_suite.EES, EES 7.210, 13/13); tools/compare_solution.py, no unit conversion (already SI Pa, C, J)
verification.notes: No common variable exceeds rtol=0.001. compare_solution.py prints 5.06e-05 for both V_dot_su and v_su. Unrounded, V_dot_su is the maximum at 5.057521e-05 and v_su is 5.057469e-05. CoolProp Air gives v_su = 1.030541406 m3/kg against the EES stored 1.030593528 m3/kg. M_dot is fixed by the similarity laws before the property call, so V_dot_su = M_dot*v_su carries that specific-volume difference. rpm differs by 1.98e-10 and M_dot by 1.09e-10. A second compare_solution.py run with --ees-units converted no reference value and rewrote no name (the units column is empty). The equations were not changed. t_su = 50 was left in Celsius; the stored solution has t_su = 50 and CoolSolve matches it. The system is square with both t_su/T_su and p_su/P_su left as written.
